reasoning: Iowa’s current Senate race is being treated as a Toss Up by Cook Political Report after moving it from Lean Republican, while recent polling still shows Republican Ashley Hinson narrowly ahead of Democrat Josh Turek. The most recent public poll I found within the last 45 days, Emerson College/Nexstar, has Hinson up 48% to 45% (+3 R), but the broader race signal has shifted to essentially even. Iowa’s statewide Cook PVI is R+6.

sources.name: The Hill
sources.details: Emerson College/Nexstar found Ashley Hinson leading Josh Turek 48% to 45% in Iowa’s U.S. Senate race, a 3-point Republican edge.

sources.name: Bleeding Heartland
sources.details: Coverage of the Emerson poll said Hinson was slightly ahead of Turek, 47.5% to 45.0%, indicating a narrow Republican advantage.

sources.name: Des Moines Register
sources.details: Cook Political Report moved Iowa’s open Senate seat from Lean Republican to Toss Up, signaling the race is now effectively even rather than clearly favoring either party.

sources.name: Axios
sources.details: Axios reported that Cook shifted Iowa’s Senate race to Toss Up from Lean Republican, reinforcing that the race has become highly competitive.

sources.name: CNN
sources.details: CNN quoted Cook Political Report saying Iowa’s Senate race is now a toss-up, which implies no meaningful current partisan edge.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI Map and District List
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide PVI list gives Iowa a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+6.
